name: EIC Accelerator
status_note: Rolling cut-off dates through 2026. Check the current cut-off on the official page before preparing.
amount_detail: Grant component below €2.5M, plus equity investment from €0.5M to €10M. Total 2026 budget: €634M.
who: Start-ups and SMEs developing innovations with potential to create new markets or disrupt existing ones.
catch: Highly competitive, and the equity component means the EIC Fund takes a stake. Expect a long process.

name: EIC Transition
status_note: Deadline 16 September 2026. Only open to applicants who already received EIC Pathfinder, ERC Proof of Concept or eligible Horizon Europe funding.
amount_detail: Grants up to €2.5M. Total call budget: €100M.
who: Teams turning results from earlier EU-funded research into a commercial proposition.
catch: You cannot apply cold. Prior EIC Pathfinder, ERC PoC or eligible Horizon Europe funding is a hard gate.

name: EIC Pathfinder
status_note: Part of the EIC 2026 Work Programme. Calls open in defined windows — check the current one.
amount_detail: Grants up to €2.5M for early-stage, high-risk technology research.
who: Research teams and deep-tech ventures at the earliest, pre-commercial stage.
catch: This funds science, not go-to-market. If you have a product and customers, Accelerator fits better.

name: EIC STEP Scale Up
status_note: Part of the EIC 2026 Work Programme.
amount_detail: Equity-only funding from €10M to €30M. Total budget: €300M.
who: Later-stage European companies scaling strategic technologies.
catch: Equity only — no grant component. This is for companies already at significant scale.

name: Eurostars
status_note: Runs in recurring calls. Check the live window on the official site.
amount_detail: Funding for collaborative international R&D projects, disbursed through each country's national funding body.
who: Innovative SMEs running an R&D project with at least one partner in another Eurostars country.
catch: The international partner is mandatory. Rules and payout come from your national body, not Brussels.

name: Smart&Start Italia
status_note: Open-window scheme with no fixed deadline — applications assessed as they arrive, while funds last.
amount_detail: Zero-interest financing covering up to 80% of eligible costs, with a higher share and a partial non-repayable grant for startups based in southern Italy.
who: Innovative startups already registered, or being formed, with projects between €100k and €1.5M.
catch: You must be registered in the 'startup innovative' special register, which has its own requirements.

name: ON — Oltre Nuove Imprese a Tasso Zero
status_note: Open window. From 1 July 2026 support is granted as zero-rate financing only, repayable over 10 years.
amount_detail: Since 1 July 2026 the incentive is provided purely as zero-interest financing; the previous non-repayable component no longer applies.
who: New and recently formed micro and small businesses, with a focus on young people and women.
catch: The grant portion is gone as of July 2026. Guides written before that date still describe it — they are out of date.

name: Beni Strumentali — Nuova Sabatini
authority: MIMIT — Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy
status_note: Open window until funds run out. The 2026 Budget Law allocated €650M for 2026–2027.
funding_type: Interest contribution on bank finance or leasing
amount_detail: A ministerial contribution on the interest of bank financing or financial leasing used to buy new capital goods. Financing must be between €20,000 and €4M per company.
who: Italian micro, small and medium enterprises registered with the Registro Imprese.
catch: It subsidises the interest, not the asset. You still need a bank or leasing company to approve the finance.

name: NEOTEC
status_note: The 2026 call closed on 14 May 2026. A further call is expected but has not been published — do not plan around it until it is.
amount_short: Up to €250k, or €325k with a doctorate holder
amount_detail: Covers up to 70% of the eligible budget, rising to 85% if the team brings in at least one doctorate holder. Caps of €250,000 and €325,000 respectively. 2026 call total: €20.38M, with at least €5M reserved for women-led companies.
who: Small innovative technology-based companies no more than three years old, with at least €20,000 of share capital and no distributed profits.
catch: The three-year age limit is strict and counted from incorporation. Miss it and nothing else matters.

name: ENISA — Préstamos Participativos
authority: ENISA — Ministerio de Industria y Turismo
amount_detail: A participative loan underwritten on the project rather than on the founders' personal assets, so no personal guarantees are required.
who: Innovative SMEs and startups in any sector with a genuinely differentiated project.
catch: It is a loan, not a grant — it has to be repaid, and part of the interest is tied to your results.

name: Kit Digital
authority: Red.es / Acelera pyme — Gobierno de España
status_note: Segments and windows have changed repeatedly since launch. Confirm which segment is open for your company size before starting.
amount_short: Up to €29,000 depending on company size
amount_detail: A digital voucher spent with accredited providers on defined digital solutions: website, e-commerce, cybersecurity, electronic invoicing and others.
who: Existing Spanish SMEs and self-employed professionals digitalising their operations.
catch: You cannot spend it freely — only with accredited providers, on a fixed catalogue of solutions.

name: Bourse French Tech
status_note: Applications handled continuously by Bpifrance regional offices.
amount_detail: Covers the earliest expenses of validating an innovative project: feasibility work, prototyping, early market testing.
who: Companies under 5 years old with fewer than 50 employees, at the very start of an innovation project.
catch: Sized for first steps, not for scaling. Amounts are modest compared with later Bpifrance instruments.

name: Bpifrance — Aide au développement de l'innovation
status_note: Permanent scheme, assessed case by case by Bpifrance.
amount_short: Grant and repayable advance, covering part of project costs
amount_detail: Direct support for technological innovation work — development, prototyping, industrialisation — as a grant, a repayable advance, or a mix.
who: SMEs and startups with a technology innovation project of real scientific or technical content.
catch: Part of it is typically a repayable advance, not free money. Terms are negotiated per project.

name: EXIST-Gründungsstipendium
authority: BMWE — Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Energie
status_note: Applications are submitted through a partner university's startup network, not directly.
amount_short: Monthly stipend for the pre-founding phase
amount_detail: A monthly stipend covering living costs during the preparation phase, before the company is registered, plus allowances for materials and coaching.
who: Students, graduates and researchers preparing a technology or knowledge-based startup from a university.
catch: You need a university to host and sponsor the application. Without that route, you cannot apply.

name: ZIM — Zentrales Innovationsprogramm Mittelstand
authority: BMWE — Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Energie
status_note: Applications temporarily suspended from 7 July 2026, 12:00. The stop applies to all project types and to project outlines. Do not start an application until it reopens.
amount_detail: Non-repayable grants toward R&D project costs. Individual projects: maximum assessment base of €690,000. Cooperation projects run at higher rates and volumes.
who: SMEs with up to 1,000 employees, any sector, running R&D projects alone or in cooperation.
catch: Currently suspended. Most 2026 funding guides still list it as open — they have not been updated.

name: StartUP Voucher
status_note: The 4th edition closed to applications on 30 January 2026. A further edition has not been announced.
amount_detail: A monthly scholarship of €900, specialised mentoring, incubation in accredited entities, training and networking, plus interim and completion prizes.
who: Graduates up to 29 years old creating their own employment in technology-based areas.
catch: Hard age limit of 29, and the window is closed. Check for a fifth edition before planning around it.

name: Portugal 2030 — Sistemas de Incentivos (COMPETE 2030)
status_note: An umbrella of schemes (productive innovation, qualification, internationalisation) that open as separate calls. Check which call is currently open.
amount_detail: Support rates generally range from 25% to 75% of eligible investment depending on region, company size and the type of scheme.
who: Portuguese SMEs investing in productive innovation, qualification, or internationalisation.
catch: It is not one programme but several, each with its own window. 'Portugal 2030 is open' is not a useful statement on its own.

name: Interreg Italia-Francia Marittimo
status_note: Programme runs 2021–2027 with calls opening periodically. Check which call is live.
amount_short: Voucher for digital and green transition support
amount_detail: Two strands: setting up a business, and supporting existing SMEs through digital and ecological transition, typically via advisory and training vouchers.
who: Aspiring entrepreneurs and SMEs in the eligible cross-border maritime regions of Italy and France.
catch: Geographically restricted to specific coastal regions. Being in Italy or France is not enough on its own.
